# Fixture builders

Rules are data, and the tests that prove they fire are builders in this directory. A
builder assembles its trigger string at test time from fragments and writes it to a
temporary directory.

This directory never holds a live-looking payload, a real secret or a real Stellar seed,
and no fixture here is read by the scanner outside a test run. A committed payload would
turn this repository into the thing the scanner looks for.

Conventions (`project_structure.md` 5):

- Builder name matches the rule id with underscores: rule `cfg-dynamic-code` has builders
  named `cfg_dynamic_code`.
- Every rule needs one positive builder that triggers it and one negative builder that
  must not. The suite fails on a rule that has only one (task 2.12).
- Wasm fixtures are generated byte strings (`\0asm` plus a trivial section), never
  compiled contracts.
